the most effective graphical documentation is: 1) static, 2) interactive (with the exception of some tasks that require the ability to edit the program code), and 3) editable (for some tasks).

the following three classes of program understanding tasks are most likely to benefit from graphical forms of documentation: (1) tasks that require the understanding of a large number of program components (i.e. tasks that require the integration of information from a large number of source code files); (2) tasks that require an understanding of the dynamic execution of a program; and (3) tasks that require a high level of precision in the understanding of the program.
